headline: Union Environment Minister reviews Haryana's Air Pollution Action Plan with Chief Minister (Haryana)
fullText:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

Union Environment Minister reviews Haryana's Air Pollution Action Plan with Chief Minister (Haryana)

Shri Bhupender Yadav stresses Strict Enforcement, Accelerated Implementation and Whole-of-Society approach to curb NCR Air Pollution in a time-bound manner

24 JUL 2026 10:21PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, today held a comprehensive review meeting with the Chief Minister of Haryana, Shri Nayab Singh Saini, and senior officials of the State Government to assess the progress of ongoing measures aimed at improving air quality in Delhi-NCR. During the meeting, the Minister emphasized the need for accelerated implementation, stronger inter-agency coordination and strict enforcement to ensure substantial reduction in pollution levels before the onset of the winter season. Haryana Minister for Environment and Forest, Shri Rao Narbir Singh, was also present during the meeting.

Emphasizing the urgency of timely action, Shri Bhupender Yadav said, "The window before the winter season must be fully utilized to implement pollution control measures in mission mode. Timely execution, effective coordination and strict enforcement will be critical to achieving visible improvements in Delhi-NCR's air quality."

Reviewing measures to curb Road Dust, the Minister requested that end-to-end paving and greening of roads with local species shrubs/grasses during monsoons be undertaken on priority, with focused attention on pothole identification and repair, construction of footpaths and pavements, roadside greening and deep cleaning of roads.

Shri Yadav requested that all gaps in the deployment of Mechanical Road Sweeping Machines (MRSMs) be bridged by September this year. He further suggested that all MRSMs be geo-tagged to facilitate real-time monitoring of road-cleaning operations and improve accountability.

Reviewing the status of Electric Mobility, the Minister stressed that deployment of electric buses across the NCR municipal corporations in Haryana should be expedited, noting significant gaps in the existing fleet. He congratulated the Haryana Government for the rapid installation of EV charging stations across the seven municipal corporation areas under review.

On the issue of End-of-Life (EoL) vehicles, Shri Yadav requested the authorities to expedite issuance of No Objection Certificates (NOCs) for transfer of eligible EoL vehicles outside the NCR, while simultaneously encouraging scientific scrapping of old and unfit vehicles. He also called for faster replacement of old polluting vehicles with electric vehicles under the Parivartan Scheme.

The Minister requested that Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) cameras be installed at all fuel stations for effective implementation of the "No PUCC, No Fuel" initiative. Stressing the need to improve urban traffic management, Shri Yadav asked the authorities to identify Traffic Congestion Hotspots on a mission mode and implement suitable mitigation measures at the earliest.

Reviewing Industrial Pollution control measures, Shri Yadav stressed the need for accelerated installation of Online Continuous Emission Monitoring Systems (OCEMS) and Air Pollution Control Devices (APCDs) across industrial units.

The Minister reviewed progress on Construction And Demolition Waste management and requested that establishment of Secondary Collection Centres for C&D waste be expedited. He also stressed that liquidation of Legacy Waste should be undertaken on a war footing. Referring to municipal solid waste (MSW) and Biomass Burning, Shri Yadav called for the constitution of dedicated task forces and emphasized achieving 100 per cent collection of municipal solid waste and biomass to eliminate littering and prevent open burning.

On Stubble Burning, Shri Yadav requested the State Government to bridge gaps in procurement of Crop Residue Management (CRM) machinery and accelerate establishment of Custom Hiring Centres. He emphasized the need for intensive Information, Education and Communication (IEC) campaigns and farmer training programmes to promote effective use of CRM equipment. The Minister suggested that local elected representatives identify stubble-burning hotspots in coordination with Gram Panchayats. He further requested District Collectors to survey industrial units and document their crop residue storage and consumption capacities to facilitate efficient demand-supply management. The State authorities were also advised to ensure adequate availability of crop residue balers.

Underscoring the importance of public participation and coordinated institutional action, Shri Yadav said, "Air pollution can be effectively tackled only through a 'Whole of Government' and 'Whole of Society' approach". Chief Minister (Haryana), Shri Saini, directed State Government officials for timely action on different measures discussed during the meeting. He thanked the Union Minister for his valuable guidance in this matter.

The meeting was attended by the Secretary, Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change; Chairperson, Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM); senior officers of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change and the Government of Haryana. Senior officials from the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) and the Haryana State Pollution Control Board (HSPCB) were also present.

headline: Union Minister for Finance & Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman outlines 5Rs of responsive tax governance; Calls for greater tax certainty and reduced litigation at the 167th Income Tax celebrations in New Delhi today
fullText:
Ministry of Finance

Union Minister for Finance & Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman outlines 5Rs of responsive tax governance; Calls for greater tax certainty and reduced litigation at the 167th Income Tax celebrations in New Delhi today

The Union Finance Minister reiterates fair, efficient, transparent and taxpayer-centric administration

Income-tax Act, 2025 and new rules and forms mark landmark reforms towards simpler and taxpayer-friendly tax system: Revenue Secretary Shri Arvind Shrivastava

CBDT Chairman Ravi Agarwal highlights progress in faster return processing, grievance redressal and litigation reduction

CBDT advances technology-led tax administration through PAN 2.0, ITBA 2.0, IEC 3.0 and SAKSHAM NUDGE

FM Smt. Sitharaman releases six publications highlighting India's growing leadership in international taxation and taxpayer-centric governance

24 JUL 2026 9:23PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Finance & Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman participated in the 167th anniversary of Income Tax Day celebrations by Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) in New Delhi today.

Shri Arvind Srivastava, Secretary, D/o Revenue; Shri Ravi Agrawal, Chairman, CBDT; Shri Vivek Chaturvedi, Chairman, CBIC: Members of CBDT and CBIC and other senior officers and officials of the Department were present on the occasion.

Addressing the 167th Income Tax Day celebrations, Union Finance Minister Smt. Sitharaman emphasised that the role of the Income Tax Department has evolved from tax collection to building a fair, efficient, transparent and taxpayer-centric tax administration. She described the implementation of the Income-tax Act, 2025 as a landmark reform that has simplified the law, reduced compliance costs and strengthened ease of doing business. She also highlighted the enhanced capacity of the e-Filing portal, improved return processing, prompt refunds and significant progress in grievance redressal, while stressing that the Department must move beyond disposal of grievances to analysing recurring issues and preventing them through systemic improvements. She outlined the 5Rs of Responsive Tax Governance - Recognise, Respond, Redress, Reflect and Reform, as guiding principles for taxpayer service, emphasising that honest taxpayers should experience convenience, opportunities to correct bona fide errors and a tax administration that exercises its authority with humility. Stressing that taxpayers are partners in India's development, she called for a continued focus on reducing litigation by strengthening tax certainty.

FM Smt. Sitharaman also underlined the importance of strengthening institutional capacity through modern infrastructure, technology and continuous investment in human capital. She appreciated the progress made in upgrading offices and welfare facilities and called for greater capacity building in emerging areas such as artificial intelligence, data analytics, forensic accounting, international taxation, transfer pricing, digital assets, cybersecurity and leadership development. She urged the Department to deepen voluntary compliance, further simplify the taxpayer experience, strengthen tax certainty, harness technology responsibly, build institutional excellence, reinforce public trust and embrace continuous improvement. Congratulating the officers and staff of the Income Tax Department on the occasion of the 167th Income Tax Day, she expressed confidence that the Department would continue to play a pivotal role in promoting ease of doing business, strengthening taxpayer confidence and supporting India's economic growth.

In his address on the occasion, Shri Arvind Shrivastava, Secretary, D/o Revenue, Ministry of Finance, extended his greetings to the officers and officials of the Income Tax Department and described the implementation of the Income-tax Act, 2025 and the new Income-tax Rules and Forms as landmark reforms towards a simpler, clearer and more taxpayer-friendly tax system, and appreciated the Department's efforts in strengthening taxpayer outreach, grievance redressal, litigation management and technology-driven service delivery. Emphasising the need to leverage technology while keeping taxpayers at the centre of reforms, he called for continued focus on ease of compliance, tax certainty, quality service delivery and innovation, and expressed confidence that the Department would continue to strengthen public trust and contribute to the vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047.

Welcoming the dignitaries on behalf of the Income Tax Department, Shri Ravi Agrawal, recalled the priorities set out by the Union Finance Minister during the previous Income Tax Day celebrations and the expectations articulated at the PRARAMBH programme earlier this year, he outlined the Department's progress over the past year in translating those directions into measurable outcomes. He highlighted the Department's sustained efforts towards reducing litigation, faster disposal of appeals and enhancing tax certainty through Advance Pricing Agreements.

He also noted the achievements in the areas of expeditious return processing, appeal-effect orders and refunds, and strengthening grievance redressal. He further highlighted the Department's achievements in expanding taxpayer outreach through initiatives such as PRARAMBH and Samvaad. He also underscored the Department's continued focus on leveraging technology through initiatives such as PAN 2.0, ITBA 2.0, IEC 3.0, Kar Saathi and the SAKSHAM NUDGE framework to simplify compliance, improve taxpayer experience and strengthen voluntary compliance. He expressed his appreciation to all CBDT verticals, including the Exemptions vertical, and the officers involved in framing the Rules and Forms under the Income-tax Act, 2025. Expressing gratitude for the continued guidance and support of the Hon'ble Finance Minister, he reaffirmed the Department's commitment to building a fair, transparent and trusted tax administration through innovation, collaboration and citizen-centric governance.

The Union Finance Minister also released six flagship publications of the Income Tax Department, reflecting its continued commitment to knowledge sharing, capacity building, transparency and taxpayer-centric governance. These included:

Avlokan, the inaugural Annual Report of the FT&TR Division highlighting India's growing leadership in international taxation;

The Manual on Exchange of Information; the updated Guidance Note on FATCA & CRS;

India's first comprehensive Guidance Note on Crypto Asset Reporting Obligations for Crypto-Asset Service Providers;

The Annual Report of the APA Programme, showcasing the programme's progress; and

Re-engineering Tax Governance, tracing the Department's journey of transformation from paper-based processes to an integrated, technology-driven and taxpayer-centric digital ecosystem.

Four short films showcasing the history of taxation, the Karmyogi Shiksha Path Portal, achievements of Income-Tax department in FY 2025-26 and the reimagining of taxpayer communication in the digital age were also screened during the event.

The function ended with a vote of thanks proposed by Smt. G. Aparna Rao, Member, CBDT. She thanked the Union Finance Minister for gracing the occasion and inspiring the Department with her words of wisdom. She also thanked all the other dignitaries present on the occasion. She also thanked the media and organisers of the event.

headline: Department of Telecommunications Activates Intra-Circle Roaming (ICR) in Affected Districts of Nagaland, Gujarat, UT of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu amid Heavy Rainfall and Flooding
fullText:
Ministry of Communications

Department of Telecommunications Activates Intra-Circle Roaming (ICR) in Affected Districts of Nagaland, Gujarat, UT of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu amid Heavy Rainfall and Flooding

Swift measures taken to ensure uninterrupted telecom connectivity and support emergency operations across disaster-affected region

24 JUL 2026 8:03PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) has taken immediate and proactive measures to ensure the continuity of essential communication services across disaster-affected regions in Nagaland, Gujarat and the Union Territory of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu. Continuous heavy rainfall, landslides, flash floods, and severe inundation have caused extensive damage to critical telecom infrastructure, leading to large-scale network outages and disrupted transmission routes in these areas.

To mitigate communication breakdowns during rescue and relief operations, DoT has invoked emergency response mechanisms under the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)-2020 for Telecom Services in Response to Disasters and the Unified Licence provisions:

Nagaland (Longleng District): Following incessant rainfall, landslides, and multiple Optical Fiber Cable (OFC) cuts, Longleng becomes the second district in Nagaland after Mon to have ICR activated. Directions have been issued to activate ICR immediately upto 23:59 hrs of 27th July, 2026 or till further instructions, whichever is earlier.

Valsad district of Gujarat, Dadra & Nagar Haveli district and Daman district of UT: Severe flooding has caused major node outages across Dadra & Nagar Haveli, Daman, and adjoining Valsad district. DoT has authorized immediate activation of ICR Immediately upto 23:59 hrs of 27th July, 2026 or till further instructions, whichever is earlier.

The activation of ICR enables mobile subscribers of any provider as well as visiting in-roamers to seamlessly access any available network in locations where their home network is temporarily offline. This ensures optimal utilization of surviving telecom infrastructure and maintains vital connectivity for affected residents, emergency responders, healthcare personnel, and disaster management agencies.

The Department of Telecommunications is continuously monitoring network status through its field units and working with all service providers to expedite full restoration of communication networks in the affected districts.

What is ICR & how to use it:

Intra Circle Roaming (ICR) is a telecom arrangement where a mobile subscriber connects to another operator’s network within the same telecom circle (region). This allows users to access mobile services even if their own operator has no coverage in that specific area. It plays a critical role during natural disasters when mobile infrastructure is damaged.

During the time of disaster, if mobile infrastructure is damaged in a region, DoT issues instructions to Telecom Service Operators to implement ICR.

To ensure ICR works:

Keep "Automatic Network Selection" enabled in your phone settings.

If automatic connection fails;

Go to Settings>Mobile Networks>Network Operators

Manually select another available network

headline: DEVELOPMENT OF INLAND WATERWAYS AND RELATED PROJECTS
fullText:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways

DEVELOPMENT OF INLAND WATERWAYS AND RELATED PROJECTS

24 JUL 2026 7:46PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India has embarked upon a transformational drive to promote Inland Water Transport (IWT) as a key pillar of India's multimodal transport system under Maritime India Vision 2030 and Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047. The primary objective encompasses creating world-class waterway infrastructure through fairway development, multimodal terminals, community jetties, river cruise terminals, regional centres of excellence, digital navigation tools, and green vessel technologies, coupled with seamless integration under the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan.

The development and regulation of National Waterways (NWs) are spearheaded by the Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI), an autonomous organization under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways. To improve the Ease of Doing Business and simplify approvals, IWAI has introduced an array of digital reforms:

PANI: Portal for Asset and Navigation Information to facilitate seamless navigation planning.

Jalyan & Navic Portal: A centralized database and digital portal developed on the lines of 'Vahan' and 'Sarathi' for nationwide online registration of vessels and crew, enabling accurate tracking and strategic planning.

CAR-D: Cargo Data Portal for real-time tracking and logistics data integration.

Jal Samriddhi Portal: Dedicated portal supporting commercial and operational activities across National Waterways.

Digital Charts and Hydrographic Surveys: Modern hydrographic charts provided digitally to Mariners for enhanced safety.

These infrastructure, digital, and policy reforms have resulted in the operationalization of 32 National Waterways across the country, laying the foundation for a technology-driven, sustainable, and globally competitive IWT ecosystem that reduces logistics costs, promotes green mobility, and accelerates inclusive economic growth.

LOGISTICS EFFICIENCY & ENVIRONMENTAL COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS

Inland Water Transport serves as an economic and environmentally friendly alternate mode of transport to Rail and Road, significantly reducing congestion on existing transport networks.

Economic Freight Cost Comparison (2014 Price Baseline)

Inland Water Transport (IWT): Rs. 1.06 per Ton-Kilometer (TKm)

Railways: Rs. 1.36 per Ton-Kilometer (TKm)

Highways (Road): Rs. 2.50 per Ton-Kilometer (TKm)

(Source: Ministry of Railways, TTSS, and IWAI)

Environmental Impact & Emission Analysis

Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Emissions: IWT emits 0.0006 Rs/TKm, on par with Railways (0.0006 Rs/TKm) and significantly lower than Roadways (0.0031 Rs/TKm).

Air Pollution Costs: IWT accounts for 0.03 Rs/TKm, compared to 0.0366 Rs/TKm for Railways and 0.202 Rs/TKm for Roadways.

Noise, Soil & Water Pollution: IWT has negligible impact on noise, soil, and water pollution, whereas Road transport incurs 0.0032 Rs/TKm (noise) and 0.005 Rs/TKm (soil/water).

(Source: 12th Five Year Plan, Planning Commission TTS Study, PIANC)

POLICY MEASURES & SECTORAL REFORMS

Jalvahak Scheme: A scheme providing 35% financial incentive to cargo owners and scheduled operators for cargo movement on NW-1, NW-2, and NW-16 via the Indo-Bangladesh Protocol (IBP) route by Inland & Coastal Shipping Limited (ICSL). Approved at a budget of Rs. 95.42 Crore for 3 years.

Tonnage Tax Extension: Announced in the Union Budget on 01.02.2025, extending the special taxation system under the Indian Vessels Act, 2021 to inland vessels operating on NWs, rivers, and canals. Tax is calculated based on vessel size (tonnage) rather than net profit, ensuring stable, predictable, and lower tax burden.

National Waterways Regulations 2025: Notified to provide a transparent regulatory framework that encourages private sector capital investment in building and operating inland waterways terminals and jetties.

Cargo Aggregation & MMLPs: To resolve multimodality challenges arising from lack of industrial concentration along river banks, Multi-Modal Logistics Parks (MMLP) at Varanasi and Integrated Cluster-cum-Logistics Park at Sahibganj are being developed through NHLML (MoRTH). Rail connectivity to 3 MMTs is assigned to M/s Indian Port and Rail Company Ltd.

PSU Cargo Shift Mandate: Over 140 Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) across key ministries (Petroleum & Natural Gas, Co-operation, Fertilizer, Food & Public Distribution, Heavy Industries, Steel, and Coal) have been engaged to mandate cargo allocation and modal shift to waterways.

The Coastal Shipping Act, 2025: Enacted to modernize regulation at par with international standards, expand vessel chartering entities, reduce compliance burdens, and foster ease of doing business. Effective from 15.03.2026.

Coastal Cargo Promotion Scheme: Announced in Union Budget 2026–27 to increase the share of Inland Waterways and Coastal Shipping from 6% to 12% by 2047.

headline: Two Days of the BRICS Science Academies Forum Meeting 2026 successfully concluded at IIT Hyderabad with focus on AI for Sustainability and Global South Cooperation
fullText:
Ministry of Science & Technology

Two Days of the BRICS Science Academies Forum Meeting 2026 successfully concluded at IIT Hyderabad with focus on AI for Sustainability and Global South Cooperation

24 JUL 2026 7:32PM by PIB Delhi

The Day 01 of the BRICS Science Academies Forum Meeting 2026 with the focal theme “Harnessing Artificial Intelligence for Sustainable Development and Strengthening Global South Cooperation” commenced today at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Hyderabad, bringing together member and participating countries from BRICS to deliberate on the 3C’s Collective, Collaborative and Context sensitive approaches towards Artificial Intelligence (AI). The forum witnessed the presence of 08 BRICS member countries - Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Russia and South Africa along with 05 BRICS partner countries - Nigeria, Vietnam, Belarus, Kazakhstan and Malaysia.

Delivering the Presidential Address of the host academy - Indian National Science Academy (INSA), Prof. Shekhar Mande, President of INSA, underscored the transformative role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in addressing priority global and global south challenges, and also emphasized the importance of ensuring that AI systems remain ethical, inclusive, transparent and accessible to all socio-economic fabric of the society. Dr. Debashis Mitra, Vice President (International Affairs), INSA delivered the context-setting address, underlining the urgency for strengthened multilateral scientific engagement. This was followed by an institutional address by Prof. B. S. Murty, Director of IIT Hyderabad who focussed on the various AI associated programmes undertaken at IIT Hyderabad.

Key Focus Areas of AI Collaboration

The deliberations identified five priority verticals for AI-driven interventions:

Advanced Materials and Manufacturing: Accelerating materials discovery, enabling smart manufacturing and optimizing supply chains.

Healthcare: Enhancing clinical decision-making, enabling population-scale screening and advancing health research.

Climate Change and Environmental Sustainability: Improving long-term forecasting, integrating AI with physical models and enabling risk mitigation.

Agriculture and Food Security: Providing AI-powered advisories, accelerating seed research and leveraging digital public infrastructure.

Disaster Prediction and Management: Strengthening forecasting capabilities, seismic analysis and resource optimization during emergencies.

The thematic focus of the Forum was introduced in the Statement Overview session led by Prof. Ambuj Sagar, IIT Delhi and set the stage for detailed deliberations. Representatives from participating academies presented their national perspectives and engaged in substantive discussions.

Brazilian Academy of Sciences emphasized inclusive AI for healthcare, climate resilience and food security

Chinese Academy of Sciences highlighted data sharing, validation and evidence-based policymaking aligned with SDGs.

Academy of Scientific Research and Technology, Egypt called for capacity building and a BRICS AI Network

Ethiopian Academy of Sciences stressed preservation of linguistic diversity alongside cybersecurity and AI education.

Indonesian Academy of Sciences underlined explainability, ethical risks and the need for AI to augment human judgement.

Russian Academy of Sciences advocated trusted AI systems with strong ethics, transparency and institutional mechanisms such as Centres of Excellence.

Academy of Science of South Africa focused on addressing the digital divide and prioritizing climate, health and food security.

The Nigerian Academy of Science emphasized ethical AI and data-driven planning.

Vietnam Academy of Science and Technology raised concerns on employment, local data and environmental impacts.

National Academy of Sciences of Belarus highlighted telemedicine and data security

National Academy of Sciences of the Republic of Kazakhstan stressed technology access, SDG alignment and support for young scientists.

Summarizing the deliberations, Prof. U. B. Desai, Vice President (Fellowship Affairs), INSA highlighted the need for enhanced cooperation, capacity building and knowledge exchange among member countries. The day also featured a Plenary Lecture by Prof. Anurag Agrawal, Vice President (Science Policy), INSA on the topic “Why AI in healthcare? (And When Not to Use It).” The formal proceedings of Day 01 concluded with discussions, followed by a cultural programme and networking dinner.

The second day of the BRICS Science Academies Forum Meeting 2026 concluded initiated with a plenary lecture by Prof. Indranil Manna, Vice President (Science & Society), INSA. He highlighted the role of AI in materials discovery, including data collection, pattern extraction, physics-based modelling and identification of promising material candidates. The keynote lecture by Dr. Ashish Lele, Director, CSIR-NCL, focused on “Harnessing AI and Green Hydrogen: Driving Efficiency and Decarbonization.” He outlined India’s energy transition pathway, the importance of the National Green Hydrogen Mission and the need for greener logistics and decarbonized data centres.

A key highlight of the concluding day was the Open Discussion on the Joint Statement, chaired by Prof. Shekhar C. Mande, President, INSA, where representatives from BRICS member and partner science academies engaged in extensive deliberations to finalize a consensus communiqué. The Joint Statement, reflecting the shared vision and recommendations of the participating academies, is expected to be endorsed within a week and will be presented at the forthcoming BRICS Science, Technology and Innovation (STI) Ministerial Meeting in August 2026.

In his concluding remarks, Shri Shambhulingappa Hakki, Joint Secretary (MER & G20) and BRICS Sous Sherpa emphasized that science is an indispensable pillar of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and evidence-based public policy. Congratulating the participating academies for arriving at a consensus communiqué, he remarked that the deliberations were both timely and aligned with India's vision of human-centric development.

The proceedings concluded with a vote of thanks by Dr. Brajesh Pandey, Executive Director, INSA who expressed gratitude to all participating academies, delegates, speakers, IIT Hyderabad, MEA and INSA team for concluding the forum successfully.

headline: 'Weaves of India' Festival Showcases India's Finest Handloom Heritage at Central Cottage Industries Emporium
fullText:
Ministry of Textiles

'Weaves of India' Festival Showcases India's Finest Handloom Heritage at Central Cottage Industries Emporium

The festival is open to visitors from 24 July to 7 August 2026

24 JUL 2026 7:24PM by PIB Delhi

The Office of the Development Commissioner (Handlooms), Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, is organizing the 'Weaves of India' Festival at the Central Cottage Industries Emporium (CCIE), Janpath, New Delhi. The festival will remain open to the public from 24 July to 7 August 2026 as part of the celebrations leading up to 12thNational Handloom Day on 7th of August.

The festival presents a curated celebration of India's rich and diverse handloom traditions, bringing together exemplary handwoven creations representing 116 heritage weaves from across the country. It offers visitors an opportunity to experience the extraordinary craftsmanship, artistic excellence and cultural legacy preserved by generations of Indian weavers.

The exhibition features celebrated weaving traditions from Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Manipur, Chhattisgarh, Bihar, Telangana, Gujarat, Jammu & Kashmir and Tripura, among others. Visitors can explore iconic handloom traditions including Banarasi, Jamdani, Kanchipuram Silk, SambalpuriIkat, Paithani, Kani Pashmina, BawanButi, Kotpad, Ilkal,Kasargod, Himroo and Risha, each representing the unique cultural identity and textile heritage of its region.

Beyond showcasing exceptional textiles, the festival aims to strengthen public appreciation for authentic handwoven products while creating greater awareness about sustainable, ethical and artisan-led production systems. It also provides a valuable platform for interaction between master weavers, designers, collectors, buyers, researchers and the general public.

The Government of India remains committed to preserving, promoting and revitalising the country's rich handloom heritage through sustained support for artisans, design innovation, market development and consumer awareness. The 'Weaves of India' Festival reflects this commitment by celebrating India's living textile traditions and encouraging citizens to support the country's handloom artisans.

The festival is open to visitors at the Central Cottage Industries Emporium, Janpath, New Delhi, from 24 July to 7 August 2026. Members of the public are invited to witness the timeless elegance and unparalleled artistry of India's handwoven heritage.

headline: Five Senior Citizen Homes Inaugurated Across Five States; MoU Signed to Strengthen Elderly Welfare; Innovative Programmes Promote Inter-generational Bonding
fullText:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

Five Senior Citizen Homes Inaugurated Across Five States; MoU Signed to Strengthen Elderly Welfare; Innovative Programmes Promote Inter-generational Bonding

24 JUL 2026 7:19PM by PIB Delhi

The government continues to strengthen its commitment towards ensuring the dignity, security and well-being of senior citizens through comprehensive initiatives under the Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY). Commemorating the International Day of Older Persons (IDOP) 2025, the Department organised a series of nationwide programmes to promote healthy ageing, social inclusion, legal awareness and inter-generational bonding among senior citizens.

This information was given by Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri B.L. Verma in a written reply to Dr. Ashok Kumar Mittal in the Lok Sabha.

The nationwide celebrations highlighted the Government's sustained efforts to create an age-friendly society while encouraging active participation of senior citizens in community life. The initiatives also complemented the objectives of AVYAY by strengthening partnerships with institutions, civil society organisations and local communities.

As part of the celebrations, a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was signed with the Birla Open Minds Foundation to promote collaborative initiatives for the welfare and empowerment of senior citizens. The Department also virtually inaugurated five Senior Citizen Homes located in Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Assam, Uttar Pradesh and Jharkhand, further expanding institutional care and support infrastructure for elderly citizens across the country.

To encourage stronger family values and inter-generational engagement, the Department launched "Naitik Patham", an interactive educational game designed to promote meaningful interaction between younger and older generations. A QR Code-based initiative for Grandparents-Teachers Meetings was also introduced to foster greater involvement of senior citizens in children's educational development.

The celebrations included inter-generational bonding programmes in Jabalpur, Badaun, Chhatarpur, Navgaon, Biaora and Mount Abu, bringing together youth and senior citizens through interactive activities. In collaboration with S-VYASA, Bengaluru, yoga sessions and health camps were organised to promote healthy and active ageing among elderly citizens.

Recognising the importance of legal awareness, a special session on the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 was organised in collaboration with the National Legal Services Authority (NALSA). The programme focused on creating awareness regarding the legal rights, welfare provisions and social security measures available to senior citizens while encouraging families and communities to fulfil their responsibilities towards elderly members.

A cultural programme titled "Aradhana" was also organised to celebrate the invaluable contribution of senior citizens to society and to encourage their active participation in cultural and community life.

Through these initiatives, the Government reaffirmed its commitment to ensuring that every senior citizen lives with dignity, respect, security and access to quality care. Under the umbrella of Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY), the Ministry continues to work in convergence with State Governments, autonomous bodies and civil society organisations to build an inclusive and supportive ecosystem for senior citizens across the country.

headline: Spudding of first appraisal well, MN-DWN18-1-HD, begins in Mahanadi offshore basin
fullText:
Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas

Spudding of first appraisal well, MN-DWN18-1-HD, begins in Mahanadi offshore basin

Every metre drilled brings us closer to reducing import dependence, strengthening self-reliance and realising the vision of Viksit Bharat: Sh. Hardeep Singh Puri

25 JUL 2026 1:26PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas, Shri Hardeep Singh Puri, today marked the commencement of drilling of the first appraisal well, MN-DWN18-1-HD, in the Mahanadi Offshore Basin. Describing the occasion as "the beginning of a new chapter in India's journey towards energy security", the Minister said the commencement of drilling reflects the outcome of a decade of visionary reforms that have transformed India's exploration and production landscape.

The MN-DWN18-1-HD appraisal well being spudded today in the Mahanadi Offshore Basin is the first of four planned deepwater wells that will systematically evaluate one of India's most prospective offshore basins. The drilling programme will employ world-class deepwater drilling technology to unlock new hydrocarbon resources and strengthen India's domestic production capability.

The Minister said that over the past decade, the Government has fundamentally transformed the exploration and production ecosystem through landmark policy and regulatory reforms.

He highlighted the introduction of the Hydrocarbon Exploration and Licensing Policy (HELP), replacement of the nomination-based approach with the Open Acreage Licensing Programme (OALP), adoption of a transparent Revenue Sharing framework and the opening of nearly 99% of the erstwhile offshore "No-Go" areas for exploration. He noted that nearly 81% of India's active exploration acreage has been awarded after 2014, reflecting the confidence these reforms have inspired among investors and explorers alike.

Emphasising the importance of scientific exploration, the Minister said the Government has made sustained investments in geoscientific data generation through initiatives such as Mission Anveshan, the National Seismic Programme, the Extended Continental Shelf Survey, the National Data Repository and the Hydrocarbon Resource Assessment Study, creating one of the world's most comprehensive geoscientific databases to unlock India's frontier basins.

Highlighting the progress achieved under the Government's exploration reforms, Shri Puri said that under OALP, 172 exploration blocks covering nearly 3.8 lakh square kilometres have been awarded with committed investments exceeding USD 4.3 billion. During FY 2025-26 alone, around 674 wells were drilled, five new discoveries were made and seven discoveries were monetised.

The Minister said the Government's strategy is two-fold—discovering new hydrocarbon resources while maximising recovery from existing national assets. He added that efforts are also underway to revitalise mature producing fields through the deployment of advanced technologies and global best practices.

The Minister emphasised that India's energy future will not be secured by a single discovery but through sustained reforms, cutting-edge technology, scientific exploration and the dedication of thousands of geologists, engineers, scientists and offshore professionals.

"As we commence this first well today, we are not merely drilling into the seabed—we are drilling into India's future energy security. Every metre drilled brings us closer to reducing import dependence, strengthening self-reliance and realising the vision of Viksit Bharat," the Minister said.

Congratulating ONGC, Oil India Limited, the Directorate General of Hydrocarbons, technical partners and the entire exploration fraternity, Shri Puri expressed confidence that today's commencement of drilling would further strengthen India's offshore exploration efforts and contribute to the country's long-term energy security and goal of energy self-reliance.

headline: Indian Coast Guard Rescues 170 Persons in Extensive Flood Relief Operations Across Daman, Dadra & Nagar Haveli and South Gujarat

Indian Coast Guard Rescues 170 Persons in Extensive Flood Relief Operations Across Daman, Dadra & Nagar Haveli and South Gujarat

25 JUL 2026 12:13PM by PIB Delhi

Indian Coast Guard, working in close coordination with the civil administration, rescued 170 stranded persons in the flood-hit areas of Daman, Dadra & Nagar Haveli and South Gujarat, through 11 rescue operations conducted since the midnight of 22 July 2026 amidst incessant rainfall, severe flooding and extremely challenging weather conditions.

The operations commenced during the night of 22/23 July with the rescue of five stranded persons from Khanvel, Silvassa, followed by the evacuation of three fishermen trapped along the flooded riverbank at the Kadaiya coastal area. In one of the largest rescue missions, 60 persons stranded in the flood-affected Welspun Industrial Area, where road connectivity had been completely disrupted, were safely evacuated during the night of 23/24 July.

Subsequent operations included the rescue of seven persons from a bus stranded in floodwaters near Aero Fibre Pvt. Ltd., evacuation of ten persons from Dongri, helicopter rescue of four stranded persons from the Valsad-Pardi area, and overnight evacuation of eight persons from the Reliance Industries area.

In another significant rescue mission, the Coast Guard evacuated ten persons from the Avadh Society area, including a nine-month pregnant woman and a woman suffering from respiratory distress, ensuring their timely access to medical care. On 24 July, two Indian Coast Guard helicopters successfully airlifted 33 stranded persons from Mendar Village in Navsari district, including an individual experiencing severe chest pain who was provided urgent medical assistance.

Despite relentless rainfall, swift currents and hazardous operating conditions, Coast Guard personnel continued rescue efforts without pause, reaffirming the Service's motto of ‘Vayam Rakshamah’ (We Protect).

The Indian Coast Guard remains fully committed to supporting the civil administration and continues to maintain a high state of operational readiness to respond swiftly to any further emergencies arising from the ongoing flood situation.

25 JUL 2026 11:57AM by PIB Delhi

Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla paid floral tributes to former Lok Sabha Speaker, Shri Somnath Chatterjee in the Central Hall of Samvidhan Sadan, on his birth anniversary, today.

Members of Parliament, former Members of Parliament and other dignitaries also paid floral tributes to Shri Somnath Chatterjee in the Central Hall of Samvidhan Sadan, on this occasion.

Secretary-General, Lok Sabha, Shri Utpal Kumar Singh also paid tributes to Shri Chatterjee.

Shri Somnath Chatterjee was born on 25 July 1929 in Tezpur, Assam. A distinguished lawyer by profession, he entered active politics in 1968 and was first elected to the Lok Sabha in 1971. Over the course of an exceptional parliamentary career, he served ten consecutive terms as a Member of Parliament. On 4 June 2004, Shri Chatterjee was unanimously elected as the Speaker of the 14th Lok Sabha, a position he held with great distinction until 31 May 2009.

Renowned for his intellect, oratory, and deep commitment to parliamentary values, Shri Chatterjee played a pivotal role in elevating the quality of debates in the House. In recognition of his outstanding contributions to the Indian parliamentary system, he was conferred the Outstanding Parliamentarian Award in 1996.

During his tenure as Speaker, he introduced several key initiatives to modernize parliamentary functioning. Notably, he oversaw the launch of Lok Sabha Television (LSTV), a 24-hour parliamentary channel, in July 2006, and inaugurated the high-tech Parliamentary Museum in August 2006.

A portrait of Shri Somnath Chatterjee graces the Outer Lobby of the erstwhile Lok Sabha Chamber in Samvidhan Sadan. It was painted by Shri Manish Kumar Rao and unveiled on 10.02.2014 by the then President of India Shri Pranab Mukherjee.

fullText:
Union Minister Shri Prataprao Jadhav Urges Centre to Issue Commemorative Coin and Postage Stamp to Mark 150th Prakat Din of Sant Gajanan Maharaj

Shri Jadhav Writes to Finance, Communications and Culture Ministers Seeking National Recognition of Sant Gajanan Maharaj's Legacy

25 JUL 2026 11:54AM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Ayush, and Minister of State for Health & Family Welfare, Shri Prataprao Jadhav, has urged the Government of India to commemorate the 150th Prakat Din of the revered saint Shri Sant Gajanan Maharaj by issuing a ₹150 commemorative coin and a commemorative postage stamp.

In letters addressed to Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman, Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, and Union Minister for Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Shri Jadhav requested the respective Ministries to consider the proposal and issue necessary directions to the concerned authorities.

In his letters, Shri Jadhav highlighted that Shri Sant Gajanan Maharaj, who first appeared in Shegaon in Maharashtra's Buldhana district in February 1878, occupies a revered place in the spiritual and cultural heritage of Maharashtra and India. Since then, Shegaon has evolved into one of India's prominent pilgrimage centres, attracting devotees from across the country and abroad.

Shri Jadhav noted that the life and teachings of Sant Gajanan Maharaj continue to inspire generations through their message of spirituality, devotion, compassion, selfless service and human welfare. The saint's life and teachings are chronicled in the revered religious text Shri Gajanan Vijay, which holds a special place among his followers.

The Minister further highlighted the significant contribution of Shri Gajanan Maharaj Sansthan, Shegaon, in the fields of education, healthcare, rural development, social welfare and humanitarian service, reinforcing Shegaon's identity as a centre of spiritual and community service. He added that the proposed initiative would serve as a fitting national tribute to Shri Sant Gajanan Maharaj and honour the faith and sentiments of millions of devotees inspired by his life and teachings.

In his communication, the Minister also recalled the visit of the President of India to Shegaon on 25 February 2026 to inaugurate the National Arogya Fair organised under the aegis of the Ministry of Ayush. He noted that the President's visit further underscored Shegaon's importance as a centre of spirituality, culture and public service.

The Minister expressed confidence that the proposal would receive favourable consideration and provide fitting national recognition to the enduring spiritual and cultural legacy of Shri Sant Gajanan Maharaj.

The 150th Prakat Din of Shri Sant Gajanan Maharaj will be observed on 17 February 2028, marking an important spiritual and cultural occasion for devotees across the country.

The programme provided participants with first-hand exposure to the socio-economic landscape, cultural heritage and developmental aspirations of India's frontier regions, while fostering community participation, national integration and a deeper understanding of the strategic importance of border villages.

headline: Start-up Village Entrepreneurship Programme
fullText:
PIB Backgrounder

Start-up Village Entrepreneurship Programme

Catalysing Rural Economies through Grassroots Entrepreneurship

25 JUL 2026 10:12AM by PIB Delhi

The Start-up Village Entrepreneurship Programme supports non-farm enterprises through training, finance, mentoring, and community-led institutional support. By June 30, 2026, SVEP had supported 4.32 lakh rural enterprises across the country. The programme has strongly focused on social inclusion and equitable access to entrepreneurship opportunities. Around 86% of entrepreneurs belong to SC, ST, Minority, and OBC communities. Through SHGs, CRP-EPs, bank linkages, and convergence with schemes like Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana, SVEP has expanded its outreach. SVEP has emerged as an effective grassroots model for poverty reduction, local employment generation, and rural economic development.

Enterprise-Led Rural Transformation in India

India has the third-largest start-up ecosystem in the world. It has thrived with the support of favourable government policies and has proven highly beneficial for the economy's growth. However, most of the Indian start-up ecosystems are based in urban areas. Hence, the government has launched several initiatives to promote entrepreneurship and innovation in rural areas. One of the key initiatives is the Start-up Village Entrepreneurship Programme (SVEP).

Launched in 2016, SVEP is a sub-scheme of the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM). The programme supports Self Help Groups (SHGs) and their family members in establishing small enterprises in the non-farm sector. It provides financial assistance, institutional support, business management training, soft skill development, and business development services. This promotes sustainable livelihoods and self-employment opportunities in rural areas.

SVEP also facilitates access to banking linkages and convergence with government schemes. The strategic focus has been on achieving long-term economic growth and wider social benefits. A key feature of SVEP has been community-based decision-making for funding and supporting enterprises locally.

Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – National Rural Livelihoods Mission

The Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana–National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) is one of the world’s largest livelihood initiatives. It mobilizes rural poor households into Self-Help Groups (SHGs), predominantly women. The focus is on providing them with sustainable livelihoods, access to financial services, and skill development. As of mid-June 2026, more than 10.29 crore rural households have been mobilized into SHGs under DAY-NRLM.

Scaling Rural Entrepreneurship Across India

SVEP has adopted an all-inclusive approach, with a strong focus on supporting women, marginalized communities, and individuals with limited educational attainment. Since its inception till June 15, 2026, the programme has supported over 4.32 lakh rural enterprises. Assam, Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal and Madhya Pradesh have recorded the highest number of enterprises supported under the programme.

From SHG Member to Rural Business Leader

Ms. Bhagyashri Londhe from Jahanpur, Maharashtra, began her journey by joining an SHG in 2014. Participation in SHG and Village Organization (VOs) activities strengthened her leadership and business skills. She began her entrepreneurial journey by producing small-scale quantities of masala, papad, and pickles. A ₹45,000 Community Enterprise Fund loan under SVEP enabled her to scale up production by leveraging locally sourced raw materials. Her entrepreneurial efforts gained recognition at Mahalaxmi Saras 2019-20, where she earned ₹5 lakh in revenue within ten days.

Her aspirations to learn and grow enabled her to upgrade her business knowledge and skills. She completed her Class 10 education through an open university while managing her enterprise. Training under NRLM and Krishi Vigyan Kendra enhanced her business literacy and technical capabilities. Consequently, her enterprise started producing large volumes daily, generating regular income, and creating employment for rural women. Her journey demonstrates how entrepreneurship, continuous learning, and institutional support can transform aspiring women into successful business leaders.

To support the continued expansion of SVEP, the government has released a cumulative central share of ₹942.09 crore up to February 2026. This is nearly 738% higher than the cumulative ₹112.39 crore released between the programme's launch in 2016 and January 2018.

Roadmap for Nurturing and Scaling Rural Enterprises

SVEP is implemented through the State Rural Livelihoods Missions (SRLMs), with a provision of ₹6.50 crore per block and an average investment of ₹27,083 per enterprise.

At the block level, Block Resource Centres–Enterprise Promotion (BRC-EPs) coordinate programme implementation. Trained Community Resource Persons–Enterprise Promotion (CRP-EPs) provide technical assistance to the Block Resource Centres on enterprise promotion. Banks extend financial support to eligible entrepreneurs. Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and their federations help identify potential entrepreneurs. Community institutions facilitate enterprise establishment and provide handholding support. They also manage loans through the Community Enterprise Fund (CEF). Community institutions also regularly monitor enterprise performance and growth. Digital tools support business planning, loan appraisal, and enterprise tracking. This integrated mechanism ensures effective implementation and enterprise development.

CRP-EPs are selected jointly by SRLMs and Project Implementing Agencies through testing, training, and certification. Preference is given to local residents with basic business and mathematical skills. At least 90% of CRP-EPs are selected from SHG households, with women constituting a minimum of 60% of the cadre. Each CRP-EP provides mentoring, training, and credit facilitation support to up to 50 enterprises.

From SHG Member to Best Performing CRP-EP

Ms. Poonam from Uttar Pradesh overcame social and financial barriers to become a successful CRP-EP. After joining a Self-Help Group, she was introduced to SVEP and completed a 54-day CRP-EP training programme. The training equipped her with skills in enterprise promotion and livelihood development. After completing her training, she began supporting nearly 40 enterprises by assisting with business planning, facilitating access to credit, establishing market linkages, and providing ongoing mentorship. Poonam credits SVEP for her financial independence and values the opportunity it has given her to help others establish and grow their businesses. Her journey reflects how community-based institutions and entrepreneurship support can strengthen rural livelihoods and advance women’s economic empowerment.

Entrepreneurs are identified by community institutions based on need, poverty status, and entrepreneurial potential. Beneficiaries receive training, mentoring, and financial support after enterprise viability assessment, with final loan approval provided by community-based organisations. The programme mandates that at least 60% of beneficiaries are women, while ensuring representation of persons with disabilities and SC/ST/minority communities.

SVEP is monitored at the State and Central levels through quarterly reviews and periodic assessments. Further, there is a centralized MIS system for tracking enterprise performance, fund utilisation, and programme progress.

Impact of SVEP on Rural Livelihoods and Entrepreneurship

The Quality Council of India (QCI) conducted a mid-term evaluation of the SVEP for the Ministry of Rural Development, with major field assessments undertaken in 2019. The review assessed the programme's impact on rural enterprises, livelihoods, and social inclusion.

The findings indicate positive outcomes in income generation, enterprise development, and empowerment of vulnerable communities:

99% of SVEP-supported enterprises were profitable.

SVEP enterprises contributed 57% of total household income.

Average monthly enterprise revenue was about ₹39,000.

Manufacturing enterprises recorded the highest average revenue at ₹47,800 per month.

96% of entrepreneurs reported increased savings.

75% of enterprises were owned or managed by women.

SVEP helped entrepreneurs earn incomes above their initial aspirations. Improved access to finance enabled entrepreneurs to establish and grow enterprises. Continuous mentoring strengthened enterprise management and sustainability.

Moreover, SVEP encouraged women and disadvantaged communities to become first-generation entrepreneurs. Beneficiaries reported improved confidence and livelihood security. Many households experienced better education, nutrition, health, and sanitation outcomes. Entrepreneurs gained stronger business management and financial skills. Increased savings and reinvestment supported long-term enterprise growth. The programme also enhanced the social standing of beneficiaries within their communities.

From Welfare to Enterprise-Led Development

SVEP has demonstrated that rural entrepreneurship can act as a powerful driver of inclusive economic growth when supported by strong community institutions. By empowering women, SC/ST communities, and first-generation entrepreneurs, the programme has transformed local aspirations into sustainable enterprises. This further leads to higher incomes, increased savings, and improved household well-being. More importantly, it has shown that entrepreneurial talent exists in every village and can flourish when provided with the right ecosystem. As India advances towards becoming a global start-up hub, programmes such as SVEP are laying the foundation for a vibrant rural start-up ecosystem. It is generating employment, strengthen local economies, and unlock new opportunities for millions of rural families. In conclusion, this is contributing to the vision of a self-reliant and developed India.

headline: BUCHAREST UNIVERSTY OF ECONOMIC STUDIES CONFERS HONORARY DOCTORATE ON THE PRESIDENT
fullText:
President's Secretariat

BUCHAREST UNIVERSTY OF ECONOMIC STUDIES CONFERS HONORARY DOCTORATE ON THE PRESIDENT

DEEPEN COOPERATION THROUGH JOINT RESEARCH AND FACULITY AND STUDENT EXCHANGES: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU TO ROMANIAN UNIVERSITIES

24 JUL 2026 11:01PM by PIB Delhi

The Bucharest University of Economic Studies conferred an Honorary Doctorate on the President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu, at a ceremony held in Bucharest, Romania today (July 24, 2026).

In her acceptance address, the President thanked the Rector, Senate and entire university community of the Bucharest University of Economic Studies for this recognition. She accepted the honour as a reflection of the enduring friendship between the peoples of India and Romania.

The President said that education has been the single most transformative force in her life. She stated that she had the privilege of working as a teacher and experienced first-hand how a single classroom, however modest, can change a family's future, and also whole community's future in course of time. She underlined that education is not merely a means of individual advancement, but the foundation of a just and inclusive society.

The President said that the friendship between India and Romania is based on mutual respect, trust and shared democratic values. Education has been one of the strongest pillars of this partnership. For decades, Romanian Universities have welcomed Indian students, particularly in medicine, engineering and technology. She urged the Bucharest University of Economic Studies and other Romanian educational institutions to deepen cooperation through joint research and faculty and student exchanges.

The President said that today, as the world is being reshaped by artificial intelligence, digital technologies and other rapid scientific advances, universities like the Bucharest University of Economic Studies have even greater responsibility to ensure that wisdom, ethics and compassion guide knowledge.

The President told students that they are the architects of tomorrow's world. Success is measured not only by professional achievement, but also by the values they uphold and the positive difference they make in the lives of others. She advised them to remain curious in their pursuit of knowledge, confident in their abilities and compassionate in their actions. She urged them to use their talents to build bridges across cultures and contribute to a more peaceful and prosperous world.

The Bucharest University of Economic Studies is Romania's foremost institution for higher education in economics, business and public administration. Established in 1913, it was the first university in Romania dedicated exclusively to economic sciences and has since educated generations of economists, policymakers, business leaders and public administrators. The Doctor Honoris Causa is the university's highest academic distinction, awarded to eminent personalities for exceptional contributions to academia, public service and international cooperation.

headline: “Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath” Inscribed in the UNESCO World Heritage List
fullText:
Ministry of Culture

“Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath” Inscribed in the UNESCO World Heritage List

25 JUL 2026 6:04PM by PIB Delhi

Today, in a remarkable decision taken at the 48th Session of the World Heritage Committee being held at Busan, South Korea, India’s official nomination for 2025-26 cycle, “Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath” got inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List, becoming India’s 45th property to receive this recognition. This global accolade celebrates India’s enduring cultural legacy, showcasing its diverse traditions of architectural brilliance, regional identity, and historical continuity.

Tweet by UNESCO/Hon’ble HCM/Hon’ble PM

Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Hon’ble Union Minister of Culture Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat along with Hon’ble Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh Shri Yogi Adityanath lauded the historic milestone and congratulated the people of India for this achievement.

Indian Delegation giving thanks speech at 48th COM at Busan

Ancient Buddhist Site, Sarnath

The inscribed serial property comprises two component parts – Chaukhandi Stupa and the Archaeological Remains of Sarnath (Dhamekh Stupa, Dharmrajika Stupa, Mulagandgakuti Vihara, Ashokan Pillar, etc.) – located within Varanasi in Uttar Pradesh. Together these two components preserve the architectural and archaeological remains of the ancient site of Sarnath, known in the Buddhist tradition under different names – Rishipatana, Ishipatana, Mrigadava. They all refer to a sacred geography, where the Buddha visited in the 6th century BCE and delivered his first sermon known as the “Turning of the Wheel of the Law” (Dharmachakra pravartana). This event marked the inception of the Buddhist sangha and the establishment of the principles of the Noble Eightfold Path.

Indicated by the Buddha himself to be one of the four key sites of Buddhist pilgrimage, Sarnath developed over centuries through royal, monastic and lay patronage. Numerous stupas, temples and viharas were constructed around what is believed to be the place of the first sermon of Gautama Buddha and the site where he met his first disciples. Having seen decline in the 12th century CE and subsequent destruction, it fell into obscurity until its re-discovery in the 18th century.

The site comprises an ensemble of ancient monuments constructed from the pre-Mauryan period (5th-4th centuries BCE to 3rd century BCE) up until the destruction of Sarnath in the 12th century CE (with some later additions).

Sarnath has been one of the most extensively excavated sites by the Archaeological Survey of India which resulted in a stratified settlement spread across 16 centuries (5th-4th centuries BCE to 12th century CE).

Excavations at the Archaeological remains of Sarnath, 1907-1908

(Source-Archaeological Survey of India)

After the declaration of Sarnath as the World Heritage Property, three of the four most significant Buddhist Pilgrim sites; i.e. Lumbini (Nepal), Mahabodhi Temple, Bodhgaya (Bihar) and now Sarnath (Uttar Pradesh) are now included in the World Heritage, along with several other important Buddhist sites such as Sanchi, Nalanda, Ajanta (all three in India), Anuradhapur (Sri Lanka) Paharpur (Bangladesh), Taxila and Takht-i-Bahi (both in present day Pakistan), etc.

Sarnath as a UNESCO World Heritage Property

The ancient site of Sarnath was included in the Tentative List of World Heritage in 1998. The proposal to include the site in the list of World Heritage was sent to the consideration of World Heritage Committee in Jan 2025 and after a rigorous eighteen-month long process involving several technical meetings with the advisory bodies and visit of ICOMOS’s mission to review the site, this historic decision was taken by the members of the World Heritage Committee today evening at Busan, South Korea.

ICOMOS technical evaluation mission examining the excavated staircase at Sarnath during 24 to 29 September 2025

Bird-eye view of the Excavated remains at Sarnath

During the Committee Meeting, the 21 Members of the World Heritage Committee, Member States, UNESCO Secretariat, World Heritage Centre, and Advisory Bodies of UNESCO (ICOMOS, IUCN, ICCROM) congratulated the delegation of India for this momentous occasion.

The “Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath” is nominated under criteria (iii) and (vi), recognizing enduring spiritual significance of Sarnath Cr. (iii), one of the four principal destinations of Buddhist pilgrimage, as demonstrated by the large number of religious buildings and other monuments that were built and rebuilt on-site during the many centuries of its existence and through Cr.(vi) direct and tangible way to the events in the life of the Buddha that are of outstanding significance to the Buddhist community – his first sermon and meeting of his first disciples. The importance of these events and their meaning is carried by the numerous constructions erected at Sarnath over the centuries, which are a response to the message of the Buddha, his teachings, and the concept of Triratna.

View of excavated Ashoka pillar and Lion Capital with the Mulagandhakuti Vihara, 1904-06 (Source-Archaeological Survey of India)

Excavated Ashokan Lion Capital, 1904-06 later declared as the National Emblem (Source-Archaeological Survey of India)

The purpose of including these heritage sites in UNESCO’s list is to preserve and promote shared heritage based on OUVs (Outstanding Universal Values) found in cultural, natural as well as mixed properties across 196 countries. On its part, India became a member of the coveted World Heritage Committee from 2021-25 and also hosted for the first time the World Heritage Committee Meeting in July 2024 at New Delhi.

Scientific Preservation Works underway on the brick votive Stupas at Sarnath

This global recognition is a testimony to New India’s relentless pursuit of highlighting Bharat’s heritage on the world forum. This recognition underscores the conservation and management efforts of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) in preserving these historic treasures.

For over 150 years, the Archaeological Survey of India has been excavating and conserving the Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath, leading to the discovery and identification of Sarnath with the place where Shakyamuni Buddha gave his first Sermon.

The famous Mauryan Lion Pillar which later became the National Emblem of India and the Dharkachakrapravartan Buddha from the Classic Gupta Art were found from the excavations which are presently displayed at the India's earliest site Museum which was established in 1904.

World Heritage status would reinforce India's identity as the birthplace of Buddhism and enhance cultural diplomacy with nations such as Japan, Thailand, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Cambodia, Vietnam, South Korea, Mongolia, etc.

This recognition would further support India's efforts to promote Buddhist heritage as a bridge for international engagement and would also showcase India's expertise in heritage conservation and preparedness in nomination process.

Last year, ‘the Maratha Military Landscapes of India’ were inscribed in the World Heritage List at the 47th Session of the World Heritage Committee held at UNESCO Headquarters at Paris.

With 45 sites in the List, India ranks 6th globally and 2nd in Asia Pacific Region for the most number of World Heritage Sites. 196 nations have ratified the World Heritage Convention, 1972.

India also has 69 sites in the Tentative List of the World Heritage, which is a mandatory threshold for any site to be considered as a World Heritage property in future. Every year, each State Party may propose just one site for consideration of the World Heritage Committee for inscription to the World Heritage List.

On behalf of the Government of India, Archaeological Survey of India is the nodal agency of all the World Heritage related matters in the country.

With this global recognition, India affirms its commitment to protect Sarnath's Outstanding Universal Value by Manage tourism sustainably and prevent unplanned development in the buffer zone in order to preserve authenticity and integrity of the property.

headline: From Mines to Markets: How MoRTH's Kanpur–Kabrai Highway Will Transform Logistics and Agriculture
fullText:
Ministry of Road Transport & Highways

From Mines to Markets: How MoRTH's Kanpur–Kabrai Highway Will Transform Logistics and Agriculture

25 JUL 2026 5:40PM by PIB Delhi

Kanpur–Kabrai (4/6 Lane Access-Controlled) Highway, approved earlier this month by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA), is set to emerge as a transformative infrastructure project for Central India. To be implemented by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) under the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH), the 117.7-km greenfield highway, with an estimated cost of ₹7,145 crore, forms a vital part of the Bhopal–Kanpur Economic Corridor. The project will strengthen logistics, enhance industrial connectivity and improve market access for farmers by seamlessly linking Bundelkhand's mineral-rich areas, industrial clusters and agricultural hinterland with major consumption centres. By enabling faster and more efficient movement of minerals, manufactured goods and farm produce, the corridor is expected to reduce logistics costs, improve supply chain efficiency, attract investment, generate employment and drive inclusive regional development. More than a transport corridor, it represents a strategic investment in connecting mines to markets and unlocking Bundelkhand's economic potential.

Powering Central India's Logistics Network

The Kanpur–Kabrai Highway will significantly improve freight mobility across Bundelkhand by providing a high-speed, access-controlled corridor linking the Kabrai mining belt—one of North India's leading sources of aggregates and construction materials—with major industrial and urban centres, including Kanpur and Bhopal. Faster and more reliable movement of mineral resources will lower transportation costs, reduce fuel consumption and improve operational efficiency for freight operators.

The project will also decongest existing highways, enhance the reliability of industrial supply chains and support seamless movement of goods across the region. Travel time between Kanpur and Kabrai is expected to come down from around 3.5 hours to nearly 1.5 hours, improving freight turnaround and strengthening linkages with PM Gati Shakti economic and logistics nodes, thereby creating a stronger foundation for industrial growth and investment.

Expanding Market Access for Farmers

Beyond strengthening logistics, the highway will improve market access for farmers across Bundelkhand by enabling faster transportation of agricultural produce to mandis, processing units and consumption centres. Shorter travel times will help preserve the quality of perishable commodities, reduce post-harvest losses and lower transportation costs, allowing farmers to realise better value for their produce.

The improved corridor will also facilitate easier movement of seeds, fertilisers, farm machinery and other agricultural inputs, enhancing farm productivity while integrating rural producers more closely with regional and national markets. Better connectivity is expected to create new economic opportunities across the agricultural value chain and contribute to higher rural incomes.

Driving Regional Prosperity Through Infrastructure

The Kanpur–Kabrai Highway reflects MoRTH's commitment to building world-class transport infrastructure that serves as a catalyst for economic transformation. By integrating mining regions, industrial clusters and agricultural hinterlands with major growth centres, the project will strengthen supply chains, improve the ease of doing business and stimulate investment across Bundelkhand. As a critical component of the Bhopal–Kanpur Economic Corridor, it will promote balanced regional development, generate employment and lay the foundation for a more connected, competitive and prosperous Central India.

headline: Delhi's Underground Link to the Future: The Tunnel Set to Rewire the Capital's Connectivity
fullText:
Ministry of Road Transport & Highways

Delhi's Underground Link to the Future: The Tunnel Set to Rewire the Capital's Connectivity

25 JUL 2026 5:37PM by PIB Delhi

For millions arriving in India's capital each year, the first impression of Delhi is often shaped by congested airport approaches, traffic bottlenecks and lengthy journeys between key business, diplomatic and cultural districts. The 6 Lane Dwarka Road Tunnel on NH- 148AE, approved earlier this month by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) is set to redefine urban mobility in the National Capital Region. To be implemented by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) under the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH), the 8.1-km, six-lane project, to be developed at an estimated cost of ₹6,969.67 crore on Hybrid Annuity Mode (HAM) under the NH(O) Scheme, will connect the Shiv Murti Interchange on the Dwarka Expressway (NH-248BB) with Nelson Mandela Marg in Vasant Kunj. The corridor will provide a high-speed, access-controlled link between West and South Delhi, particularly benefiting traffic from Gurugram, Dwarka, IGI Airport and West Delhi. Its defining feature is a 3.14-km twin-tube tunnel, including a 1.98-km stretch beneath the Southern Ridge, ensuring seamless mobility while preserving one of Delhi's most ecologically sensitive landscapes.

Reimagining Urban Mobility

The Dwarka Tunnel Corridor will provide a direct, uninterrupted connection between the Dwarka Expressway and South Delhi, reducing dependence on heavily congested routes such as Dhaula Kuan–IGI Airport–Mahipalpur, Chhatarpur–Mahipalpur and Rangpuri. By improving traffic flow and reducing travel delays, the project will make daily commuting faster, safer and more reliable for residents, airport users and commercial traffic alike.

The corridor will also strengthen integration between Delhi and Gurugram, improving access to key residential areas, commercial centres, institutional hubs and the Indira Gandhi International Airport. Together with NHAI's proposed AIIMS–Mahipalpur Elevated Corridor, which will connect the tunnel to the Barapullah Elevated Road, the project will establish seamless east-west connectivity across the city, benefiting travel to East Delhi, Ghaziabad and Noida while creating a more efficient urban transport network.

Enhancing Tourism and Visitor Experience

Delhi welcomes millions of domestic and international visitors every year, and efficient connectivity is central to their travel experience. The Dwarka Tunnel Corridor will improve access from the airport and the Dwarka Expressway to several of the capital's iconic destinations, including Qutub Minar, Mehrauli Archaeological Park, Hauz Khas Heritage Complex, Humayun's Tomb, Lodhi Garden and Chhatarpur Temple. It will also facilitate smoother travel to Bharat Mandapam, India Gate and other major venues that host international conferences, exhibitions and cultural events.

By reducing congestion around the airport corridor and major traffic bottlenecks, the project will offer visitors a faster, more comfortable journey while supporting Delhi's hospitality, tourism and meetings, incentives, conferences and exhibitions (MICE) ecosystem.

Strengthening Delhi's Global Gateway

As the primary gateway to the National Capital, the Indira Gandhi International Airport serves millions of passengers each year. The new corridor will improve connectivity between the airport and Delhi's diplomatic enclave, business districts, convention centres and institutional hubs, enabling quicker and more predictable travel for international delegates, business travellers and investors. By strengthening links between the airport, Dwarka, Gurugram and South Delhi, the project will reinforce Delhi's position as a leading centre for commerce, diplomacy and global engagement.

Building Sustainable Infrastructure

A distinguishing feature of the project is its environmentally sensitive design. The 3.14-km twin-tube tunnel, including a 1.98-km section beneath the Southern Ridge, enables critical transport infrastructure to be developed while preserving Delhi's valuable green cover and minimising surface disruption. This approach reflects MoRTH's commitment to balancing infrastructure development with environmental stewardship.

More than an urban road project, the Dwarka Tunnel Corridor represents a strategic investment in future-ready mobility. By improving connectivity, reducing congestion and integrating key transport corridors, it will enhance the quality of urban life, strengthen economic activity and support the continued growth of the National Capital Region.

headline: DRI intensifies crackdown on gold smuggling; seizes 27 kg smuggled gold in intelligence-led nationwide operations; 12 arrested
fullText:

DRI intensifies crackdown on gold smuggling; seizes 27 kg smuggled gold in intelligence-led nationwide operations; 12 arrested

25 JUL 2026 4:01PM by PIB Delhi

Continuing its sustained crackdown on organised gold smuggling syndicates, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has carried out a series of intelligence-driven operations across the country, resulting in the seizure of over 27 kg foreign-origin smuggled gold and the arrest of 12 persons. The operations exposed sophisticated concealment methods, including concealment inside aircraft lavatories, specially fabricated cavities in vehicles and utensils, and body concealment, highlighting the evolving modus operandi adopted by organised smuggling syndicates.

Acting on specific intelligence, DRI officers at Mumbai intercepted three passengers on 23-24.07.2026 arriving from Addis Ababa and, after an extensive search of the aircraft, recovered 6 foreign origin gold bars weighing around 12 kg concealed inside the ceiling panels of the rear lavatory of aircraft. Investigation revealed that the passengers had concealed the gold for subsequent retrieval by airport staff. The gold was seized and all three passengers were arrested.

On 23.07.2026, acting on specific intelligence, officers of DRI intercepted a female passenger travelling on the Brahmaputra Mail in Uttar Pradesh and recovered 42 foreign origin gold bars weighing around 5 kg concealed in a waist belt and inside her handbag. The passenger admitted that the gold had been smuggled into India through Bangladesh. The gold was seized and the passenger was arrested.

In another intelligence-led operation at Mumbai Airport during 22-23.07.2026, DRI officers unearthed a smuggling syndicate again using aircraft lavatories for concealment of gold dust in wax form, which was subsequently retrieved by compromised aircraft cleaning staff. The operation led to the seizure of 3.7 kg gold dust in wax form and the arrest of five persons, including the carrier, cleaning staff, handler and recipient.

On 19-20.07.2026, officers of DRI intercepted a passenger at Kolkata Railway Station and recovered 4.6 kg foreign-origin gold, ingeniously concealed inside specially fabricated utensils. Investigation revealed that the contraband had been smuggled into India through Myanmar. The gold was seized and the passenger arrested.

During the week, in two more separate operations, DRI officers at Cochin and Guwahati seized around 2 kg foreign-origin gold. At Cochin Airport, gold concealed inside the body of a passenger arriving from Dubai was recovered, while at Guwahati, gold biscuits concealed inside a specially fabricated cavity in a car were seized. Two persons were arrested in these operations.
